**Next: [B] CTF-B02 — Astra: attraction of the scalar carrier**
Prepared for Edward Baker with substantial LLM assistance, gpt-6-astra / ultra, 29 October 2026.
Continue in `/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity`, investigation `papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry`.
Read the root research/model workflow, result and avoid indexes, current Overview05/Progress05, Notes89–91, Review45, Reference16, and the latest E08 R13 disposition. If that assessment remains pending, keep the dependence on R13 explicit. Preserve Sol’s manuscript integration.
**The unresolved question**
Determine whether the state-dependent scalar feedback admits an attraction mechanism strong enough to prove convergence of the actual carrier toward the stationary candidate identified in Note90.
The actual carrier satisfies\
[\
h_s=\mathcal N(h)+\mathfrak f_s,\qquad\
\mathcal N(h)=\Delta h+\beta(h)\operatorname{div}(vh),\
]\
where\
[\
\beta(h)=\frac{2|\nabla h|\_2^2}{\int d h^2},\
\qquad\
\mathfrak f_s=(\alpha-\beta(h))\operatorname{div}(vh).\
]
R13 pays the feedback defect and an integrable forcing tail in the specified **dual-Lipschitz test seminorm**. It also proves\
[\
|h(s)|\_2^2\longrightarrow E_0/n,\qquad n=\mu^2/M^2.\
]
The unique smooth radial stationary candidate at this mass and energy is\
[\
h\_{\lambda\_*}=\frac{M e^{-\lambda\_*\mathcal V}}{Z(\lambda\_*)},*\
*\qquad*\
*\mathcal V(r)=\frac{r^2}{2}+\frac12\log(1+r^2),*\
*]*\
*with*\
*[*\
*\frac{Z(2\lambda\_*)}{Z(\lambda\_\*)^2}=\frac{E_0}{\mu^2}.\
]
These results do **not** establish attraction, convergence of either feedback coefficient, or shadowing by an independently evolved scalar solution.
**The bounded conceptual task**
Select and test one concrete Lyapunov, contraction or stability mechanism for this scalar feedback. The intended consumer is convergence of the actual carrier toward (h\_{\lambda\_\*}), preferably in (L^2). A limit for (\alpha) requires its own derivative control.
First resolve the structural issue: classical fixed-drift Fokker–Planck entropy does not automatically remain monotone when the coefficient is (\beta(h)). Note90’s conditional entropy identity displays the unpaid term. Likewise, common-path contraction cannot compare the actual carrier with a stationary profile driven by a different coefficient.
Pay every compactness, regularity, weighted-moment or Fisher-information assumption the chosen argument needs. If transferring the forcing requires a stronger topology, prove that additional estimate or identify it as an explicit missing cost.
Give the direct comparator identical information. Retain the known physical-mass premise, unchanged source and feedback, genuine residual, preparation mismatch, sphere terms and entire inner ball. A generic attraction theorem would be useful auxiliary-flow progress; it would not itself remove the physical-mass assumption or establish a theta-specific collision exclusion.
**Completion and continuation**
Record the selected mechanism in Progress05 before substantive testing. Return one complete argument, one precisely scoped failed route, or a fixed **[E] CTF-E07 — Sol** contract once the remaining proof steps are specified.
Stop at that boundary. Do not begin a parameter scan, alter the PDE, infer convergence from equilibrium uniqueness, or expand the manuscript during this conceptual task.
Save research notes, an appropriately qualified review, progress and chat history. End with research guidance and a model-continuation note. Preserve existing chat identities; a model change does not provide independent specialist review.

The continuation note from the Sol work is here: /papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/93_COMPLETE_CARRIER_R13_ASSESSMENT_AND_MODEL_CONTINUATION_20261029.md

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder. Please provide guidance for the continuation at the end of your research, and a continuation note for model changes.\

R13 has been accepted without mathematical correction in Review46. Its forcing estimate is still only in the dual-Lipschitz seminorm. I’m checking a fixed-candidate entropy mechanism against the actual state-dependent coefficient; the test must either control the extra term or establish a precise reason this route fails.

The entropy calculation exposes a concrete obstruction. Mass and squared \(L^2\) norm do not fix the sign of the feedback contribution. I’m checking an exact mass-and-energy-preserving construction that makes entropy production positive, with finite regularity, moment and Fisher-information costs. This would rule out this global entropy route, without deciding whether the actual theta carrier converges.

The sign obstruction is stronger than a large-data example: the construction can be made arbitrarily close in \(H^1\) to the stationary candidate, at exactly the same mass and energy, while entropy production stays positive. It does not show nonconvergence of the actual carrier. I also found short deductions that pay an \(H^{-1}\) forcing bound and spatial \(L^2\) compactness; those still leave the stationarity step unresolved.

The bounded test is complete: fixed-candidate entropy fails as a universal attraction mechanism, including near equilibrium in \(H^1\). The actual forcing and Fisher-information costs can be paid, so they do not resolve this sign obstruction. I’m saving the proof, qualified review and continuation guidance, with Sol’s manuscript preserved.

This defeats universal entropy monotonicity; it does **not** disprove attraction of the actual carrier.
